title: TSMC OIP Ecosystem Forum 2026: Opening Remarks - Semiwiki
gist: At TSMC's 2026 OIP Ecosystem Forum, executives said the semiconductor industry has passed $1.7T (vs a prior ~2030 $1T expectation) with AI infrastructure spend near $1T this year, argued for a shift from DTCO to system-level STCO, and introduced a TSMC AI Design Kit (ADK) to support agentic AI design flows that may replace parts of traditional CAD.

insights.claim: TSMC North America CEO Sajiv Dalal said the semiconductor industry has crossed the $1.7 trillion mark and AI infrastructure spending reached roughly $1 trillion this year, with investment expected to grow dramatically over the next several years.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Industry scale and AI capex claims support continued foundry and equipment demand.
insights.quote: an industry that has now crossed the $1.7 trillion mark and to AI infrastructure spending that he said reached roughly $1 trillion this year

insights.claim: TSMC's Lipen Yuan called this a 'golden era' for semiconductors, noting an industry once expected to hit $1 trillion around 2030 has moved far faster on AI demand and is now approaching $1.7 trillion.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Industry growth far ahead of prior forecasts implies upside to capacity and capex plans.

insights.claim: Dalal said AI is moving rapidly to the edge, accelerating drug discovery, diagnostics, autonomous vehicles, manufacturing and warehousing.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Edge AI broadens demand beyond hyperscale data centers.

insights.claim: TSMC highlighted nanosheet technologies, advanced stacking and packaging, next-generation HBM base die, backside power delivery and integrated voltage regulation as innovations for AI performance and power efficiency.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Maps TSMC's AI-era technology roadmap and associated ecosystem opportunities.

insights.claim: Yuan said the industry can no longer optimize individual chips in isolation; future AI platforms need system-wide co-design across logic, packaging, memory, interconnects, power delivery, cooling and networking, moving from DTCO to STCO.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: System-level co-optimization favors vertically broad ecosystems and multi-physics tool vendors.
insights.quote: the industry can no longer optimize individual chips in isolation

insights.claim: AI workloads are driving enormous compute demand while straining memory bandwidth, interconnect performance, power consumption, cooling and system efficiency.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Bottlenecks point to growth in memory, interconnect, power and cooling suppliers.

insights.claim: TSMC's 3DFabric Alliance brings together memory, EDA, test, OSAT and other partners to address thermal, mechanical and integration challenges in complex multi-die systems.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Packaging ecosystem partners are increasingly central to TSMC's AI value chain.

insights.claim: TSMC's executives argued collaboration across the ecosystem will determine how quickly and successfully AI's growth opportunity becomes reality, with OIP spanning nearly two decades of foundry, EDA, IP, cloud, design services and packaging partnerships.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: TSMC's ecosystem breadth reinforces its competitive moat versus other foundries.

insights.claim: TSMC says it is already seeing meaningful productivity gains from AI-assisted semiconductor design.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: AI-in-EDA is producing real gains at the leading foundry.

insights.claim: TSMC introduced the TSMC AI Design Kit (ADK), complementing traditional PDKs and EDA flows, to support emerging agentic AI design methodologies.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: A foundry-backed agentic design standard could reshape EDA workflows and vendor dynamics.

insights.claim: TSMC envisions engineering teams building orchestration layers of AI agents and specialized skills that work alongside, or potentially replace portions of, traditional CAD flows.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Potential disruption risk for incumbent EDA tool revenue models.
insights.quote: work alongside—or potentially replace portions of—traditional CAD flows
